items.claim: The imperative-driven scene shift at the span's opening and the confirmed ketiv/qere and paseq disclosures at its middle verse are byte-accurate, and the disclosed medium_low confidence appropriately reflects the genuinely unresolved question of exactly where second-person address to Moab begins.
items.evidence: Re-derivation against the staged WEB text confirms the quoted wording at the span's open and close matches source exactly. The ketiv/qere and paseq inventory confirms both a ketiv/qere pair and a paseq fall at Jer.48.27 exactly as disclosed (single-witness, count-only, correctly not used as an intra-verse position claim), and no other disclosure-bearing mark exists inside the span that was left unmentioned. The rejected alternative is not a strawman: it is candidly held open rather than dismissed, conceding the drunkenness figure and the Israel-comparison could argue either boundary. The opening imperative, addressed to an unnamed third party rather than to Moab directly, is a real but modest register shift following a place-name judgment catalogue in the preceding material rather than a macro-level formula onset, and the medium_low rating matches that evidentiary weight rather than overclaiming it.

items.claim: The quoted WEB wording at three internal attribution points renders the source's curly quotation marks as straight ASCII quotes, breaking the mandatory curly-quote convention even though the underlying words are otherwise verbatim.
items.evidence: Byte comparison against the staged WEB verse text shows the source pairs curly quotation marks around the Yahweh-attribution clause in the middle of Jer.48.30 and again in the middle of Jer.48.35, and closes with a single curly quotation mark at the end of the reported material in Jer.48.38. This span's own quotation of each of these three verses substitutes a straight double-quote character at those positions, and at Jer.48.38 additionally appends an extra curly closing quotation mark after the verse's final word that the source itself does not carry there. The wording is not otherwise altered, and the neum-YHWH analysis is sound apart from this: the mid-verse instances at Jer.48.30 and Jer.48.35 are correctly held as non-driving, and the instance closing Jer.48.38 is correctly read as corroboration only, since no fresh tier-1 onset follows until Jer.48.40. The closing setumah is confirmed present at Jer.48.39 exactly as disclosed, with no other disclosure-bearing mark inside the span left unmentioned.

items.claim: Two of the span's WEB quotations render the source's curly quotation marks as straight ASCII quotes, the same verbatim-fidelity defect as its immediate neighbor, even though the tier-graded inclusio, the ketiv/qere disclosure, and the exegesis-note disclosure elsewhere in the span are all byte-accurate.
items.evidence: Byte comparison against the staged WEB verse text shows the source opens Jer.48.40 with a curly quotation mark immediately after the introductory clause, and closes Jer.48.43 with a curly quotation mark immediately before the closing attribution; this span's quotation of both verses substitutes a straight double-quote character at those two positions. Independently, the exegesis-note and ketiv/qere disclosures at Jer.48.44 check out exactly against the inventory, which lists both a ketiv/qere note and an exegesis note at that verse and no other disclosure-bearing mark anywhere else in the span. The self-magnification clause comparison between Jer.48.42 and Jer.48.26 is correctly tier-graded to the consonantal/skeleton level, with the cantillation difference between the two sites named rather than glossed over. The koh-amar onset at Jer.48.40 is adequately warranted independent of the quotation defect: it is corroborated by the setumah closing the immediately preceding verse, a register shift from lament back to judgment-oracle, and imagery explicitly disclosed as unused earlier in the oracle.

items.claim: The vocative interjection opening the span is correctly distinguished from the book's other woe lexeme, and the byte-attested terminus clause closing the span is quoted verbatim and correctly scoped to the whole Moab oracle rather than only to this span, with the paragraph fold at the close properly disclosed as non-evidentiary.
items.evidence: The staged WEB text confirms both quotations verbatim, including the terminus sentence, and confirms that the span's closing verse carries a live paragraph-continuation fold, consistent with its own disclosure that the fold is tier-4 layout metadata and not argued as boundary evidence. The parashah inventory confirms a setumah at the span's closing verse and no other disclosure-bearing mark inside the span. The opening interjection is confirmed distinct from the lexeme used at the book's woe-oracle onsets and funeral-cry sites, consistent with its description here as a different word from the one already cited earlier in the same nations collection. This span also closes the transition into the following nation's header-bounded material; the frame designation carries forward correctly unchanged on both sides of that transition, since the two nations share a single frame in the architecture and the transition is a header-level seam rather than a frame seam.

items.claim: The lamed-initial header opening the span is correctly identified and paired with a disclosed addressee-shift signal rather than resting on the speech formula alone, and the restraint in not fragmenting at the internal vocative shift midway through the span is a defensible reading since neither the vocative nor the formula recurs there with a genuinely new addressee class.
items.evidence: The header verse's combination of a lamed-prefixed nation name with the divine-speech formula matches the book's inventory of lamed-initial nation headers, and the closing divine-title stack is one of four such expanded stacks across the whole book, with the span's own count correctly scoped to the two that fall within this nations collection. The staged WEB text confirms the four cited quotations verbatim, including the header fragment, the vocative outburst, and the closing title-stack clause. The nearest parashah mark before the span's own opening is confirmed to fall exactly where disclosed, one chapter back, correctly typed and not conflated with the other mark class.

items.claim: The one-verse restoration coda is a well-corroborated internal seam, combining a disclosed discourse pivot, a formulaic restoration idiom independently attested at a parallel oracle-closing site later in the same nations collection, and a parashah mark falling exactly at the verse's own close.
items.evidence: The staged WEB text confirms the quoted wording verbatim at both cited fragments, and the parashah inventory confirms a setumah at this exact verse and no other disclosure-bearing mark inside so short a span. The restoration idiom is independently attested at the site named as its parallel later in the same collection, a legitimate verse-anchored cross-reference. The topical pivot from judgment to restoration is a genuine content shift rather than a bare formula repetition; although it does not by itself belong to any of the named macro seam-classes, the combination of the pivot with the corroborating mark and the structurally parallel restoration-coda pattern elsewhere in the same nations collection gives the boundary adequate multi-signal support for a single-verse unit.

items.claim: The second lamed-initial header is correctly identified and, like its neighbor, is paired with a disclosed addressee-shift signal rather than resting on the speech formula alone, and the restraint in not fragmenting at the internal narrowing from a plural to a singular addressee midway through the span is consistent with the caution against per-turn fragmentation.
items.evidence: The header verse's lamed-prefixed nation name combined with the tsevaot-form divine-speech formula matches the book's inventory of lamed-initial nation headers. The staged WEB text confirms the three cited quotations verbatim. The parashah inventory confirms the disclosed front-seam mark at the coda verse immediately preceding the span and the disclosed closing mark at the span's own final verse, both correctly typed as the same mark class, with no other disclosure-bearing mark inside the span left unmentioned. The internal narrowing from the plural address to Dedan's inhabitants to the singular address to Esau is disclosed as internal texture rather than manufactured into a further boundary, which is the sounder call in the absence of any fresh formula or scene marker at that narrowing.

items.claim: The span's only disclosed seam driver is a bare reintroduction of the divine-speech formula by the same speaker already carrying the oracle through the immediately preceding span, without a disclosed addressee, scene, or frame-owner change to justify treating the formula restart as a fresh onset rather than a continuation of the same judgment oracle against the same nation.
items.evidence: Both the opening and closing quotations match the staged WEB text verbatim, and the paseq disclosure at the opening verse is correctly handled as count-only with no intra-verse position claimed. This span's own account of the formula restart describes it as the divine-speech formula reintroducing itself after the mercy clause, which concedes there is no change of speaker: the same first-person divine voice addressing the same nation carries continuously from the mercy clause through the cup-of-wrath image to the closing oath, with the third-person cup clause functioning as a rhetorical a-fortiori comparison rather than a genuine new addressee, since direct address to the same target resumes within the same verse and continues through the close. Unlike the header-driven formula onsets at Jer.49.1 and Jer.49.7, each of which discloses an accompanying shift in who is being addressed, this boundary discloses the bare speech formula alone as its substrate signal. The setumah closing the immediately preceding verse is correctly disclosed as this span's front seam, but that mark is single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only under the Prophets ruling and cannot itself supply the frame-owner or addressee change the formula restart lacks. The rejected alternative of keeping this material within the unit that precedes it is set aside on the ground that the formula is a recognized reintroduction device used elsewhere in the book, but that reasoning does not address whether an accompanying frame-owner or addressee change is required for a formula restart to license a fresh boundary by itself.
